clue.text: Badly in love, is in this state

parts.note: badly means ill, as in 'ill-treated'
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone unhappily in love declares the condition they are in.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites 'this state' to mean a state of mind; it is one of the United States. The second 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is a Midwestern US state, so it is fairly called 'this state' in a clue about a state.

clue.text: Cast objects to cut

definitions.meaning: small cubes thrown, or cast, in games
to chop food into small cubes

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the gaming cubes that get thrown; the verb is the kitchen sense of chopping into cubes.

clue.text: First couple in Arizona initially leaving another part of US for a third

indicators.note: leaving means the letters depart from the longer state's name

parts.note: Arkansas is another US state

indicators.note: the first couple of letters, the opening pair, are taken from the word Arizona
initially reinforces that the opening letters of the word Arizona are the ones wanted

explanation.surface: A traveller seems to quit one state for another and end up in a third.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First couple in Arizona' gives AR, and 'initially leaving' takes those two letters off the front of ARKANSAS. Since Illinois and Arkansas are already in the clue's picture, the remaining state is 'a third'.
explanation.definitionFit: After Arizona and Arkansas, Kansas is a further US state, so 'a third' names it as one more state of the union.

clue.text: Tiny creatures European found in ancient part of central Asia

indicators.note: found in means one piece is discovered sitting inside the other

parts.note: Bactria was an ancient region of central Asia around the Oxus

explanation.surface: Microscopic organisms of European origin turn up in an old Asian land.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are single-celled microbes, small enough to be called tiny creatures.

clue.text: Nice column represented chaps running local government in America

definitions.text: chaps running local government in America

indicators.note: represented, read as re-presented, means the letters of these words are set out anew

explanation.surface: A newspaper column from Nice was reprinted for American town officials.
explanation.definitionFit: Councilmen is the American term for male members of a city or town council.

clue.text: In neighbourhood of Italian town I tossed off fruit drink

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about or in the neighbourhood of a figure

indicators.note: tossed off means the letter is thrown away from the town's name

parts.note: Assisi is a hill town in Umbria, home of St Francis

explanation.surface: Near an Italian town someone knocks back a fruity drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossed off' looks like drinking it down; it signals the I being dropped from the end of ASSISI.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassis is a blackcurrant liqueur, a drink made from fruit.

clue.text: Within cult, I'm a target for threats

indicators.note: within means the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A cult member complains of being singled out for menaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultimata, the Latin plural of ultimatum, are final demands backed by threats.

clue.text: Graduates left university in a minute part of UK

indicators.note: in means these two letters are placed inside the following pair

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: Former students left their university very quickly for Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A minute' looks like 'in a moment'; it gives A and M, around which LU sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former students of a school or university, i.e. its graduates.

clue.text: Open spaces in Asian city holding nothing eastern

indicators.note: holding means the city's name contains the next piece

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An Asian city with no eastern quarter has its open squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Agorae, plural of agora, were the open public squares of ancient Greek cities.

clue.text: Story about Rome's beginning as capital of Italy some time ago

definitions.text: capital of Italy some time ago

indicators.note: about means the fib is wrapped around the next letter

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of the word Rome's is taken

explanation.surface: A tale about how Rome came to be Italy's capital long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a capital city, which Rome is; here it means money, the currency Italy used before the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: The lira was Italy's currency before 2002, and capital means money, so lire were Italian money of the past.

clue.text: Small ignoramus I brought before head for indecency

indicators.note: brought before means the earlier pieces are placed ahead of the last one

parts.note: a mutt is a slang term for a fool or dimwit
a ness is a headland, as in Orford Ness on the Suffolk coast

explanation.surface: A minor dunce is hauled before the headteacher for rude behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headteacher; it is NESS, a promontory, as in Orford Ness on the English coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Smuttiness is the quality of being smutty, i.e. obscene or rude, which is indecency.

clue.text: Excited expression of character in Hamlet, not king or queen

indicators.note: not means this letter is left out of the jester's name

parts.note: of a character in Hamlet gives the possessive Yorick's, the dead jester whose skull Hamlet holds
R stands for both Rex (king) and Regina (queen)

explanation.surface: An exclamation from a figure in Hamlet who is neither the king nor the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive YORICK'S loses its R, which can stand for either a king or a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoicks is a fox-hunting cry, used generally as an exclamation of excitement.

clue.text: Fault-finding survey about old port

indicators.note: about means the survey goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a census is an official survey of the population
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port, short form Rio

explanation.surface: A survey of an old harbour town turns up lots of faults.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorious means severely critical, always ready to find fault in others.

clue.text: Son thus goes into country, returning for flowers

indicators.note: returning means the whole assembled word is read backwards
goes into means these letters are placed inside the country

parts.note: Iran is a country
sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quoted error

explanation.surface: A son heads back to his home country to pick flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses ISSICRAN, the country with S and SIC put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are daffodils and their relatives, spring flowers of the genus Narcissus.

clue.text: Private places in clubs, protected by present distributor

indicators.note: protected by means the letter sits sheltered inside the name

parts.note: Santa Claus delivers presents at Christmas
C is the card-playing abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Secluded nooks in clubs are guarded by Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Sancta, plural of sanctum, are private retreats or inner sacred rooms.

clue.text: They have parallels, giving thanks when receiving a prize in error

indicators.note: receiving means the word for thanks takes the scrambled letters inside it

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

indicators.note: in error means the letters of these words are set down wrongly, scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone gives thanks on being handed a prize by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In error' is the anagram signal on A PRIZE, and 'receiving' puts the result inside the British word for thanks. 'Parallels' points to geometry, not comparisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapezia are four-sided figures with one pair of parallel sides, in British usage.

clue.text: Priests holding mass for religious feast

indicators.note: holding means the priests contain the letter

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests or monks
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Clergy celebrating mass at a church festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Lammas is 1 August, a church festival of the first harvest loaves.

clue.text: Scaly cobras disturbed more than just me

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of the snakes are stirred into a new order

parts.note: us is a group including me and others, more than just me

explanation.surface: Scaly snakes, once disturbed, threaten more people than just the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scaly' reads as describing the cobras; it is the definition. 'Disturbed' rearranges COBRAS into SCABRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabrous means rough and scurfy-skinned, covered in scales or scabs.

clue.text: Cold unfortunately trapping one in port

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: trapping means the word encloses the numeral

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cold snap leaves someone stuck in harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the French ferry port facing Dover across the Channel.

clue.text: They work tirelessly, packing cut fruit in Gold Coast's centre

indicators.note: packing means the outer letters pack the shortened fruit inside them

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: centre means the middle letter of the word Coast's is taken
cut means the fruit loses its final letter

parts.note: the tomato is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Machines packing fruit somewhere on Ghana's old Gold Coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold Coast' looks like the old name for Ghana, but splits into the symbol for gold and the A at the centre of COAST'S; 'packing' puts the cut fruit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Automata are robots or self-operating machines, which never tire.

clue.text: Source of issue among computer users

indicators.note: among means the answer sits within the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The cause of a problem lies with the people using the computers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a computer problem; it means offspring, and the womb is where they come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means children, and the uterus, or womb, is where they develop before birth.

clue.text: Preserve vessel for oil

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
vas is Latin for vessel, used for a bodily duct

explanation.surface: Someone wants a container to keep oil in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' looks like the liquid; it is an oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil painting is a canvas in the art world's metonymy, the cloth standing for the picture.

clue.text: Operated in group with lots of intelligence — they're full of brains

indicators.note: in means this word goes inside the agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
operated means ran, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A brainy spy agency is run by people full of brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' looks like cleverness; it is espionage, pointing to the CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Crania, plural of cranium, are skulls, the bony cases holding brains.

clue.text: We want these figures about English team, right?

indicators.note: about means the figures go round the other pieces

parts.note: data are figures, numbers gathered for analysis
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A statistician queries numbers about the England team.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things needed or wanted, from the Latin for things desired.

clue.text: One part of it produces things like doughnuts

parts.note: the word it has two letters, so one part of it is either one letter or the other, read as the answer split into three pieces

explanation.surface: A single element of something makes ring-shaped things.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as T OR I describes one letter of IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tori, plural of torus, are ring shapes with a hole, the mathematical form of a ring doughnut.

clue.text: In this way, energy's extracted from so-called melting pot

indicators.note: extracted means this letter is pulled out of the phrase

parts.note: the USA is often called a melting pot of cultures, i.e. the US
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A chemist describes drawing energy from a melting pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Melting pot' looks like a crucible; it is the US, so called for its blend of immigrant cultures.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus means so, or in the manner just described.

clue.text: Unfinished clue I'm altering, about utopian's head in clouds

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round that first letter
altering means the remaining letters plus I'm are shuffled
unfinished means the last letter is dropped from the word clue
head means the first letter of the word utopian's

explanation.surface: A setter fiddles with a half-written clue while having their head in the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' trims CLUE to CLU, and 'altering' turns CLU plus IM into CUMLI, which goes 'about' the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumuli are heaped, fluffy white clouds, plural of cumulus.

clue.text: It produces reaction — litmus changes before its conclusion

indicators.note: before means the shuffled letters come ahead of the ending
changes means the letters of the word litmus are rearranged

parts.note: its conclusion is the ending of the answer itself, the Latin singular ending -us, which this puzzle's theme turns on

explanation.surface: A chemistry lesson: litmus paper changes colour before the experiment ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Its conclusion' refers to the answer itself: like many Latin nouns it ends in US, the ending the puzzle's plurals drop.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulus is anything that provokes a response in an organism or system.
